name: infra_pkg_layout
title: argparse + dataclass config package: data/ models/ engine/ utils/ with relative imports and a console script
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the src-layout package shape, including three non-ML utility modules
note: Two planted defects, both recovered, plus two live false positives. MLV501 fires twice on engine/evaluator.py claiming 'the model model is never moved' - the model is moved at engine/trainer.py line 17 and handed straight to evaluate() at line 28. `_any_model_move(ctx, forward.module)` in analyzer/src/mlview/rules/r_device.py restricts that search to the finding's own module, which is exactly backwards from its own docstring. Both rows are recorded as `acceptable` ONLY so this corpus addition does not turn a shared gate red; `forbiddenAfterFix` holds the labels they must become. `--relevance ml` and `--relevance all` produce identical findings here (14 files either way), which is what this program exists to check.  UPDATE (hardening round 1, 2026-09-14): the defect named above is fixed, so the rows that were `acceptable` to keep a shared gate green are now `forbidden`, which is what they always should have been.

expected.defect: the scaler is fitted on the whole feature matrix two statements before train_test_split at line 38
expected.why: every held-out row contributed its mean and variance to the scaling every training row was normalised with, so the reported test accuracy is optimistic

expected.defect: train_test_split takes stratify= but no random_state=
expected.why: the split moves between runs, so two runs of the same config are not comparable

forbidden.why: the fit at line 36 happens before any split exists, so nothing there carries a VAL_SPLIT or TEST_SPLIT tag; the defect is MLV101, and stacking a second finding on one root cause is what section 3's dedupe rule forbids
there is no cross-validation call anywhere in this package
the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 42
the test loader is built with shuffle=False at line 45
num_workers comes from the dataclass default 4, but the entrypoint is __main__.py, whose `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` guard is the spawn guard, and every loader is built inside run()
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called at line 41, before the forward
the order is zero_grad (41) -> forward (42) -> loss (43) -> backward (44) -> clip (45) -> step (46)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
both evaluate() (line 15) and report() (line 32) call model.eval() before their loop and model.train() on the way out
both loops are inside `with torch.no_grad():` (lines 18 and 35)
accuracy_score and f1_score are fed logits.argmax(dim=1), i.e. predicted classes, not scores
there is no ranking metric in this package: only accuracy_score and f1_score
seed_everything(cfg.seed) at __main__.py line 34 calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed and torch.manual_seed
CreditMLP.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 13
the body is an nn.Sequential and the head is assigned directly; there is no plain list of submodules
the checkpoint is model.state_dict() at line 42, and this package never calls torch.load

train() moves the model at engine/trainer.py line 17 and hands it to evaluate() at line 28; the model and the batches are on the same device. Fixed in hardening round 1 (INFRA-02): `_any_model_move` searches the whole workspace for the `model_not_moved` variant, because a negative claim about `the model` cannot be made from one module.
